en: Title: *Amoghapāśakalparāja* (7+1, 2, 3, 4) Author: Canonical Input: Péter-Dániel Szántó, 2025.ix.27 Budapest (silent corrections and standardisations)

Source: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai (Mikkyō Scripture Research Group). 2015. “*Amoghapāśakalparāja*: Preliminary Edition and Japanese Translation with Notes—Sanskrit Manuscript Ff. 97v4–99r2—. *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō* (Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University) 37: 41–68.

§1 Then Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas, said this to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara: "Speak, Blessed One! [Explain] the Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa maṇḍala and the Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya, together with the ritual procedures and the means of accomplishment. O Blessed One, perform the rite for the accomplishment of reality—the fulfillment of the hopes for success of all vidyādharas."

Then the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara said this to Vajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas: "Listen, Vajrapāṇi, I shall explain the ritual procedure for the practice. O Vajrapāṇi, for this *mūlamantra*—the secret heart-essence of the *Amoghapāśa-padmoṣṇīṣa*—whether it be a holder of the vidyā, a son of good family, a daughter of good family, a monk, a nun, a layman, or a laywoman, by merely recollecting it once, their mental attention and physical being will become completely purified through a resolute intention accompanied by great compassion and loving-kindness, directed toward all sentient beings. Not a single sentient being will be reborn in the three lower realms, nor in the domains of hell-beings, animals, or hungry ghosts; such a thing is impossible. They shall all be endowed with the great roots of merit resulting from the accomplishment of all sentient beings."
% NB *sarvasattvānālambanena* in the manuscript; should it be *sarvasattvānālambanena*?

Merely by being recited twice, it pacifies all diseases. Merely by being recited thrice, it destroys all poisons, scabies, boils, erysipelas, ringworm, leprosy, scabs, and the like. By a mere four recitations, it removes all harmful spells and *akhorda* curses. By a mere five recitations, they pacify all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes. By a mere six recitations, they destroy all fears, planetary seizures (*graha*), and fevers. By a mere seven recitations, they pacify for all sentient beings all fears of untimely death and all calamities.

Therefore, Vajrapāṇi, for the sake of all sentient beings, when [the deceased] has fallen [into a lower realm], one should recite [this mantra] seven times without speaking. O monks, whoever among all sentient beings has died destined for hell; whoever has died having broken the vows of training and moral discipline; or whoever has died having shown disrespect toward their preceptors and teachers—for their sake, one should take pure sand, empower it by reciting [the mantra] seven times, and scatter that sand upon a cemetery, a funeral pyre, or a mound. As soon as the sand is scattered, wherever those beings' bones or the grains of sand fall, there those beings who were reborn in hell, or reborn among the hungry ghosts, or born from the wombs of piśācas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas, shall instantly pass away and all become destined for heaven. They shall never again be destined for hell.

Alternatively, having written [this] on birch bark and placing it within a *caitya*, all bipeds and quadrupeds who approach that place shall have all their sinful obscurations purified by the mere falling of their shadows [upon it]. They will all become destined for heaven. Even down to animals and birds, even down to moths, mongooses, scorpions, venomous snakes, dogs, tortoises, or serpents—their all karmic obscurations shall be purified by the mere falling of their shadows there. They will all become destined for the heavenly realm.
% NB: The editors' reading "anne śarabha" is unlikely.

If one recites [this mantra] seven times over a conch shell and blows it from a high place, whatever beings hear that sound of the conch—whether they be men, women, boys, girls, wild animals, birds, or those belonging to the animal realm—they shall all become destined for the heavenly worlds. Furthermore, those beings who possess pure morality, those who delight in giving, those who observe the fast, those who uphold the three refuges, and those who are restrained by the bodhisattva vows—all of them, upon hearing the sound of the conch, shall become non-retrogressive. They shall attain unexcelled, perfect enlightenment. When they pass away and undergo the transition of birth, they will be reborn in the world-realm Sukhāvatī. And in every birth, they will be endowed with the recollection of their past lives.

§7 Having recited [the mantra] seven times over sandalwood, if one burns it as incense in a monastery, in the courtyard of a *caitya*, in the midst of the Saṃgha, in the midst of a great multitude, or in a royal palace, all those who smell that fragrance will become perfected in the body of a Buddha.

§8 By burning a robe, the obscurations of all sins of whoever wears it upon their body are destroyed. Merely by its falling upon the body, one becomes free from all stains and the fault of envy. Merely by wearing the garment, one will become a sovereign over all the world.

If one enters a royal palace while fumigating oneself with this incense, the king, along with his harem and retinue, will come under one's influence. One will become highly venerable and respected by all the world. If one enters the midst of the noble Saṅgha, one will become worthy of great veneration by all the monks. If one enters the midst of the wealthy, there will be an increase in great wealth, and one will become worthy of great honor. [Likewise] in the midst of a great assembly...

§10 If one recites the root mantra seven times while incensing the summit of the peak that faces the sun, the Sun immediately descends. He will grant the fulfillment of all desires. Incense mixed with *guggulu* should be offered before Mahādeva while reciting the root mantra seven times; while wiping [the deity] with the syllable *oṃ*, Mahādeva immediately descends and appears before the practitioner of the spell (*vidyādhara*). He fulfills every intention.

§11 Incense mixed with bola, sandalwood, and guggulu should be offered before Nārāyaṇa. With the root mantra, the mass of the body should be cleansed twenty-one times. Nārāyaṇa will appear before one in his own form and grant all boons; he even displays his universal form (*viśvarūpa*). §12 While fumigating a Brāhmaṇa with incense mixed with mustard seeds, cleansing him with the root mantra fourteen times, Brahmā will appear before one in his own form. He will become the granter of all boons.

§13 Incense mixed with lotus powder should be offered to Mahākāla together with his host of Mothers (mātṛgaṇa). Then Mahākāla, accompanied by his retinue of the Mothers, will appear before one in his own form. He will become the bestower of boons and the accomplisher of all excellent deeds. Incense should be offered in a lake inhabited by nāgas, together with *nāgapuṣpa* flowers. Having consecrated mustard seeds seven times with the root mantra, they should be thrown into the lake inhabited by nāgas. One should recollect the *Amoghapāśahṛdayasūtra* once. Then all the nāgas, nāga maidens, and nāga boys and girls will emerge from all their abodes. They will prostrate at the feet of the vidyādhara and do everything he commands; they will become subject to his will and fulfill all desires. By employing this threefold practice, even Sāgara, the king of the nāgas, will come, as will the nāga kings Nanda and Upananda. All will remain obedient and under one's control.
% Note: Reference to the *Amoghapāśahṛdayasūtra*

§14. One who desires to summon yakṣas and rākṣasas should fumigate with charcoal from a funeral pyre in the middle of a cemetery while recollecting the root mantra seven times. As he runs about with a loud voice, the yakṣas and rākṣasas arrive and fall at the feet of the vidyādhara, saying, "Command us, O Lord! Whatever the vidyādhara says according to his command must be done; they will carry out every order. They will become his servants and attendants for as long as they live. Having recited the mantra seven times over a pair of joined skull-cups, one should offer incense when the skull-cups are full; all spirits (bhūtas) will come, and they will all become submissive servants.

§15. One who desires to summon a yakṣiṇī should draw the yakṣiṇī with red ocher, prepare a maṇḍala of cow dung, and paint a white lotus. An offering (bali) should be placed upon the white lotus, and this incense should be offered. The root mantra should be recited one hundred and eight times. Having recited it seven times, the yakṣiṇī should be struck [with the mantra]. The yakṣiṇī will appear before him in her own form; she goes as far as the world of the gods and returns again. She will perform all secret tasks merely by being commanded. Alternatively, she may say, "I am your mother," "your wife," or "your sister. If she says, "I am your mother," out of maternal affection she will protect him like a prince, following after all his enjoyments and celestial palaces. If she is a sister, she will become a rival to Vaiśravaṇa in wealth. If she is a wife, she will provide him with pleasures and delights like the Lord of the Thirty-three Gods.

If one fumigates with incense for the goddess Śrī while reciting the root mantra eight times, he shall be cleansed by the goddess Śrī and stand before the Great Goddess Śrī. He shall offer vast heaps of wealth and shall attend upon him in his home for as long as he lives; there will be a great increase of riches.
If one fumigates Vaiśravaṇa, he gives a thousand pieces of gold. If one fumigates Maṇibhadra, he gives a thousand dīnāras.
§18 When one fumigates within a forest, the deities dwelling in the forest appear before one in their own forms. All medicinal substances and herbs appear before one in their own forms.
§19 When one fumigates on mountains, all grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and substances burst into flame.
§20 When one fumigates at the four city gates, or when one fumigates at all the gates, all fevers shall be liberated from them, and all strife, quarrels, conflicts, and disputes shall be pacified.

§21 For one who burns incense in the wilderness, there shall be no fear of all thieves, rogues, bandits, lions, tigers, *vyāḍas*, bears, or hyenas. There shall be no fear of any ferocious wild beasts.
§22 For one who burns incense during all fevers, they are completely liberated from all fevers.
§23 This is the third procedure for the accomplishment of the sandalwood incense rite, which removes all evil karmic obstructions.
Title: *Amoghapāśakalparāja* Author:

Canonical Source: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai. 2016. “*Amoghapāśakalparāja*. Preliminary Edition and Japanese Translation with Notes (2)—Sanskrit Manuscript Ff. 99r2–100r6—. *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō* (Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University) 38: 95–126.

Input: Péter-Dániel Szántó, 2025.ix.27 Budapest (silent corrections and standardisations) §1 Now, regarding the *tilaka*. I shall fully explain the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) for the mantra of the Kularāja.
With a splendor equal to that of the sun and endowed with a blazing form like a star,
Tejorāja shall shine forth, and his mass of merit shall increase.
For a Vidyādhara, the gods along with Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara shall always be worthy of worship; of this there is no doubt.
Thus it is said.

§2 When the *tilaka* is applied, it shines eternally upon the forehead, radiant like the sun and illuminated by a thousand-fold web of rays. Pure as crystal, with a dark-blue hue, fragrant, [with arms] like elephant trunks, with temples like those of a bull, faultless, endowed with composure and perfect self-control—it would be a unique jewel for the caravan. Recited a hundred thousand times over with mantras, this *tilaka* is easily accomplished; it blazes all around like a garment of gold.

§3. Between his eyebrows, at the center of his forehead, there is a mark that shines eternally and perpetually, like the full moon risen in the sky; it blazes amidst the people like the moon, the king of stars and constellations, and in the midst of his own kin, he blazes like Śakra, the lord of kings. Among the people, he is the sole umbrella of the world-king; like the Sugata, he is perfectly self-controlled; in the midst of the world, he is the single umbrella, and like the Śākya clan, he is a lineage seeking the welfare of all beings. Thus, O excellent jewel, he is pure and seeks the welfare of all beings. Just as the one Lord of the World, including the gods, is the supreme giver of boons for the sake of the welfare of all beings, so too is the power of the *tilaka* jewel the bestower of all desires. The gods, *nāgas*, and *yakṣas* come under his control; Indra, the lord of the thirty-three, becomes subject to his will. Upon his birth, the *gandharvas*, *asuras*, *garuḍas*, *kinnaras*, *mahoragas*, and all spirits likewise come under his control. All sentient beings are perpetually under his sway, bowing their heads at the soles of his feet. Fire does not burn him, nor does water wash him away. Poison, sorcery, *kākhorda* spells, and various wicked mantras do not assail his body. By the power of this jewel, none of these things prevail.

§4 Fever, great suffering, disease, wind-disorders, and headaches—all these are immediately pacified as if by the application of a *tilaka*. Beings imprisoned, or those deserving punishment or death, are all liberated by those who have applied this *tilaka*. Hundreds of thousands of *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas* of terrifying form, and hundreds of thousands of seizing spirits (*graha*), do not assail the body. Herds of elephants and lions, thieves, precipices, mountain falls, lightning, and the fear of cold winds, snakes, and rats—all these find peace at that very moment when the *tilaka* is applied between the eyebrows upon the forehead.

In the midst of an army of hundreds of thousands of enemies, one conquers the combatants swiftly, like a *tilaka* mark through its power; in the conduct of battle and strife, there is immediate pacification. Then, having made this *maṇibandha* [amulet] a crest-jewel on the head and a *tilaka*, one should smear it upon a discus (*cakra*) and enter into the midst of the enemy host; with a single person, one will defeat a fourfold army. As soon as one has entered with this [discus], all [the enemies] fall into calamity, flee in the ten directions, and all meet their destruction. Having made a *tilaka*, if one enters the royal court, the king together with his harem and retinue will come under one's control and attend upon him. He shall be worthy of worship for as long as he lives. Having bound the jewel on the right arm and applied the *tilaka* to every limb, one attains victory everywhere. Merely by being touched, it brings subjugation; whatever purpose one pursues, one will obtain all of that.
Having taken [the substance] from the mouth of a pill, one should address it to the "Sahasamgati" [mantra];
all [beings], including the king or even the women of the inner apartments, will come under one's control. (3)
Whether they be a śramaṇa, a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, or even a śūdra;
whether women, men, or even boys and girls—all of them become subject to one’s will for all kinds of servile tasks. (4)
As soon as this pill has been consumed, every disease is destroyed:
the quartan fever, those afflicted by wasting diseases,
and whoever suffers from chronic fever.
Wherever there is strife, as well as public hostility,
the shadow of oneself, the shadow of another, Skanda-śoṣa, apasmāra, and whatever other malevolent planetary influences there may be— || 5 ||
Those who have practiced evil deeds and whose past karma is most terrible—
all of them perish in a mere moment simply by the application of this medicinal pill and ritual bath.
In cases of glandular swellings, urticaria, erysipelas,

fistula-in-ano, spreading sores, vitiligo, leprosy, and scabies— indeed, in all those irregular and malignant afflictions caused by the bite of Vāsuki or other venomous serpents— [these remedies are effective].
As soon as it is smeared, they all immediately attain tranquility and become free from poison. || 7 ||
The divine *guḍikā* (pill) called "Reviver of the Dead" accomplishes all rites. §8 || 8 ||
For one who wears this pill or applies it as a tilaka, he receives honor everywhere and the arrival of wealth everywhere. (9)
One who desires prosperity obtains prosperity; one who seeks grain finds an abundance of grain that increases. || 10 ||
He becomes beloved of the gods and dear to the nāgas as well; he is dear to the yakṣas, rākṣasas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and all living beings. || 11 ||
One shall always be worthy of worship, and all shall remain under one's control;
all shall stand as servants and attendants—this pill should be employed. 12.
One who constantly practices the use of the medicinal pill and the forehead mark (tilaka) is attended by all the Tathāgatas; likewise,
the noble Avalokiteśvara, the granter of boons, is ever present.
At all times, one should seek the vision of a knower of reality. || 13 ||
Day by day he accumulates thousands of masses of merit;
he enjoys worldly happiness and attains supreme bliss in the next world.
Through the transformation of birth, one goes immediately to Sukhāvatī;
in whatever birth one is reborn, one always remembers one's previous lives. || 15 ||
The great yakṣa Vajrapāṇi, surrounded by ten million yakṣas, provides protection, defense, and guardianship at all times;
they guard [him] day and night without weariness. 16.
Or for one who has no son, or for a woman desiring a son, having focused the mind and recited the mantra, [the pill] should be taken in conjunction with a single pill. (17)
On the full moon of the fifteenth day of the bright fortnight, the wise man performs the ceremonial bathing of men and women by the hundreds of thousands.
One should apply the *tilaka* mark on every limb and worship the Three Jewels, while also providing a meal for a Brahmin and performing the rites of protection. (19)
One should prepare the maṇḍala for the bali offering of the three whites, adorning oneself with ornaments and putting on clean garments. || 20 ||
Abiding in a mind of loving-kindness, compassionate and fond of sentient beings, pure in your refined disposition, and always devoted to the guru. (21)
It should be strewn with various flowers and anointed with various fragrant unguents;
it should be perfumed with lamps and incense, such as turuṣka, sandalwood, and sallakī.
One should administer seven pills combined with milk and jaggery.
This secret drink, when consumed immediately, is the food that should be eaten. 23.
Worshipping the Lord Avalokita, the bestower of boons,
at the very foot of that compassionate one,
he obtains a supreme vision at dawn upon waking during the night. (24)
The noble Avalokiteśvara will show his own form as the Bestower of Boons;
that woman shall give birth to a son who grants the most excellent boon.
Handsome, most beautiful to behold, and powerful;
endowed with beauty, possessing divine splendor, and righteous—he follows [the path].
Wise, discerning, long-lived, he shall attain sovereignty.
He shall be a hero who has conquered his enemies and a crusher of all the wicked. || 26 ||

§11 Alternatively, one who desires to increase memory and intelligence should rely upon learning and remain steadfast. That *vidyādhara*, being pure, should for seven nights daily infuse seven pills with milk and ghee that have been boiled, while they are comfortably warm. Having recited the previously mentioned [mantra] twenty-one times, it should be drunk; thereafter, one should eat a meal. Within seven nights, one becomes a repository for the great ocean of learning (*mahāśrutisāgara*); all treatises—including logic (*naya*), discipline (*vinaya*), poetry (*kāvya*), grammar (*vyākaraṇa*), aphorisms (*sūtra*), prose (*geya*), verses (*gāthā*), solemn utterances (*udāna*), causal narratives (*nidāna*), historical accounts (*itivṛttaka*), birth stories (*jātaka*), the higher doctrine (*abhidharma*), enumeration (*gaṇanā*), ritual manuals (*kalpa*), mantras, and mudrās—as well as the entirety of the Mahāyāna, abide at the tip of one’s tongue.
% NB List of Genres (jāti)

§12 By practicing for three weeks, one possesses great strength, vigor, and prowess; one gains the strength of ten thousand elephants. By practicing for only a month, one lives for five hundred years, free from wrinkles and grey hair; one’s hair will become curled and ringlet-like, and one’s bodily complexion will become as fair as a lotus. By practicing for one year, the supreme divine elixir (*rasāyana*) takes effect: one wanders through the sky on an equal level with the gods, and one shall rival Śakra himself. One finds delight in the play of divine celestial nymphs and divine palaces, dwelling in mansions and palaces made of the seven jewels. Wandering while emitting a radiance like that of the sun, one moves about in excellent abodes. There is no doubt that one will become pure, blazing with irresistible splendor, and exceedingly luminous.
§13 The Fourth Ritual Procedure for the Accomplishment of the *Guḍikā* (Pill) of the *Tilaka* for the Achievement of All Rites.
Title: *Amoghapāśakalparāja*. Author: Canonical.

Source: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai. 2017. ‘Amoghapāśakalparāja. Preliminary Edition and Japanese Translation with Notes (3) —Sanskrit Manuscript Ff. 100r6–101r5—’. *Annual of the Institute for Comprehensive Studies of Buddhism, Taishō University* (*Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō*) 39: 79–97. Now, I shall truly proclaim the supreme accomplishment for the Vidyādharas— the attainment of invisibility and movement through the air, the highest of medicines, which possesses unfailing power.

§2 One should prepare a fine, auspicious, and subtle powder of *kuṣṭha*, *anavadyotpala*, excellent *padmākṣa*, *guggulu*, *parṇapa*, *patraka*, *kuṅkuma*, *nāgapuṣpa*, *gandhamāṃsī*, *śirīṣapuṣpa*, and white sandalwood, which has the fragrance of the milk-ocean of Brahmā and is as clear as crystal. Having recited the secret *Amoghapadmoṣṇīṣa* mantra eight thousand times, one should consecrate it with the *Kularāja* mantra while reciting it well-prepared. Then, while reciting the *Ekākṣara* mantra one hundred thousand times, one should consecrate it twenty-one times with the *Krodha* mantra. Furthermore, while reciting the ten *dhāraṇīs* separately from their respective mantras twenty-one times, and having fully completed the recitation of all the mantras, one should place this supreme medicine named *Amoghavipulaprabhāsa*, the size of a jujube fruit, at the feet of the Blessed Noble Avalokiteśvara, and dry it completely in the shade. Again, having recited the *Amoghapāśoṣṇīṣa* mantra eight hundred times, one should place it in a clean container; whenever there is a need, one should employ it for success in all matters and all undertakings.

Then the vidyādhara, having become pure, should put on clean garments; his body must be perfumed with well-smelled incense. He should consecrate this supreme medicine, *kaṭukatela*. While rubbing it over his own body, as soon as he has rubbed it on, he will become invisible. He sees all secret abodes with their doors wide open. He enters all those abodes at will. He shall accomplish all tasks. All *bhūtas*, *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, *piśācas*, and so forth, will become his powerful lords. They all remain under his control and attend upon him; they attend upon him for as long as he lives, remaining obedient in the performance of all ritual actions. All the abodes of the *nāgas* stand with their doors wide open; the entire retinue of *nāgas* stands before him, and they shall perform all tasks as his servants. They will carry out all duties to be done and attend upon him for as long as he lives, serving him day and night. Then all the *nāgas* will remain as executors of his commands for the rest of his life.

§4 If one prepares an antidote with the milk of a cow that has a lion’s tongue and applies it to the entire head, one will manifest various forms fashioned by one's own mind according to one's intention. One manifests them as they exist in all places. One manifests various transformed forms in the midst of an assembly, just as they exist in all locations. One manifests them for as long as life lasts and shall accomplish all tasks.

§5 By saturating *gandharva*-oil with an antidote (*agada*) and anointing one’s shanks and feet, one flies up into the air, traverses through the sky, goes wherever one desires, and walks upon water. One never again places a foot upon the ground. If one anoints the right foot, wherever that hand touches, one causes [the person] to cross over; yet no one sees this.

One should apply collyrium to the eyes. One should mix it with the milk of a woman who has borne a child once. By doing so, one may enter a royal court and become invisible. Whatever tasks one desires, he will perform them; whatever wealth or goods one takes, no one sees him. Even when there is sexual union with a woman, no one sees him. He remains under control for as long as he lives, and no one knows [his identity]. Having wiped his face, wherever he goes—whether among actors, dancers, or jesters—he will accomplish all his tasks, yet his body will not be seen.

§7 Having smeared a flask and filled it with water, a stream of water is seen, yet that [empty] vardhanikā vessel is not seen. Having filled a water-pool, while examining its center, the water is seen floating there, yet that pool is not seen. One should smear oneself; when the hand holds the flask of water, a conduit of water is seen, yet that person who is oneself is not seen.

One should anoint the eyes; having entered into the midst of a great multitude, one will become invisible. That sound will be heard, yet one's physical form will not be seen. One may enter into all places and one's physical form will not be seen, until one bathes. Whosoever one should anoint the eyes of, or smear with ointment upon their body, they shall all become invisible. Wherever one goes, there one will become hidden. By merely bathing, the restoration [of visibility] will occur.

One should smear one's entire body with it; having entered [the palace] of the Great King, one will become invisible. For whomever one so desires, taking all their gold, silver, and white silver, jewels, pearls, coral, conch shells, crystals, diamonds, lapis lazuli, emeralds, sapphire-blue gems, native gold, garments, ornaments, and decorations, one departs without anyone seeing [the act]. One shall transport [these things] wherever one wishes. As long as one does not bathe oneself, one remains invisible everywhere yet visible to all.

§10 That vidyādhara who wishes to enter the inner apartments must first bathe and become pure. Then he should be bathed with scented water; then he should be bathed with cow urine; then he should be bathed again with saffron water; then he should be bathed with the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*). Then this pill should be smeared over his body, mixed with fragrant oil. Then his eyes should be anointed with [the ointment] mixed with the milk of a young woman. Then three pills should be tied upon his right arm. Then, having put on clean garments and reciting the mantra, he should enter the royal palace; he becomes invisible and no one sees him. His body should be bathed every day, or every two days, or once a week, or twice a week, or thrice a week. There, in the midst of the inner apartments, he plays, enjoys himself, and moves about; yet no one knows it. He goes out and enters, and no one can find an opening [to catch him]. As long as he does not bathe his physical form, he will remain hidden from view.
One who desires to enter [the mandala] should bathe oneself with saffron water.

§11 Regarding the entry into a subterranean opening (*bilapraveśa*): having smeared one's entire body with fragrant oil, one should enter the opening; all the doors of the openings will become unbarred, and there one should enter the interior of the dwelling. "Perform whatever actions [you intend] exactly as they are. One may enter into the midst of water just as if it were a house, and one is not smeared by the water, nor does anyone living in the water see one there. One may enter into the midst of fire, yet the fire does not touch the body; it will become cool like sandalwood. One may enter into a lake that is a *nāga* abode, yet those dwelling in the abode do not see him. "Perform other various tasks as well. One should perform whatever action is intended in one's own mind.
§12 The Ritual Procedure for Accomplishing the Pill of Invisibility.
Title: *Amoghapāśakalparāja*. Author: Canonical.

Source: Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai. 2025. ‘Amoghapāśakalparāja. I shall now proclaim the ritual procedure for the fire oblation (homavidhi), which accomplishes all purposes and goals,
is the locus that grants all attainments (siddhis), and likewise removes all sins.
It brings about the purification of all obscurations, the unsurpassed accomplishment of all vidyās,
the pacification of all yakṣas, and the destruction of all sins.
It bestows complete victory over all Buddhas and wards off all enemies;
it is effective in quarrels, disputes, legal contests, and the cage of battle.
The accomplishment of universal deliverance is proven, supreme and unfailing, and difficult to obtain;
it is the mastery of all vidyādharas and the success of all mantra-maṇḍalas everywhere.
Through the procedure for the chapter on reality concerning the transmission of mudrās, one attains supreme accomplishment in all respects; of this there is no doubt.
It constantly bestows all happiness, it is the means for achieving all sovereign powers,
it effects the summoning of all gods, and the invocation of yakṣas and rākṣasas.
It is the crusher of all obstacles—Māras, bhūtas, piśācas, and fierce grahas;
whether it be epilepsy or terrible brahmarākṣasas, it provides deliverance everywhere. It always effects the subjugation of the siddhas, day and night, without a doubt.
Thus.
It constantly pacifies all fevers and wards off all diseases.
It destroys all poisons immediately through oblation, by means of a single dose.
They will always be beloved everywhere, their appearance will always be pleasing to all,

they will be the teachers of all the world worthy of worship, and they will possess strength, heroism, and valor everywhere; furthermore, they will constantly behold the Tathāgata— of this there is no doubt.
He will constantly and at all times look after the bodhisattvas in all activities;
and in birth after birth, he will be beloved and his speech will be authoritative.
Everywhere there is service to the guru; everywhere the guru is worthy of worship.
Furthermore, O glorious one, Vajradhara is always the protector and guardian.
And the four great kings—Yama and Varuṇa as well—[are likewise].
And there will be protection, shielding, and guarding at all times; of this there is no doubt.
Thus it is said.
§5 Īśvara and Maheśvara, along with ninety-nine thousand sons of gods possessing great supernatural power (*maharddhika*),
shall provide constant protection, defense, and guardianship, remaining ever well-restrained.
Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśvara, Rudra, Kumāra, Māṇibhadra, Baladeva, Pūrṇabhadra, and Pañcika, the best of dancers—
these shall always provide protection and defense; of this there is no doubt.
Agni, the god of great splendor, the sun, the moon, and the deities of the constellations shall provide protection, defense, and guardianship with supreme worship.
This mere fire-offering (homa) is sufficient for all undertakings among the unsurpassed accomplishments.

§7 One should offer eight thousand oblations of rice, mustard seeds, and *guggulu* resin smeared with clarified butter and honey. Noble Avalokiteśvara will become the bestower of all boons. He will be the means of accomplishment (*sādhana*) in all undertakings. Having kindled a fire with fuel-sticks of *śamī* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of sandalwood, lotus stalks, parched grain, and mustard seeds, smeared with curd, honey, and clarified butter. Thereupon, Noble Avalokiteśvara will appear before one in his own form. He will be the bestower of all boons; there will be the accomplishment of all tasks, the fulfillment of all desires, the accomplishment of all rites (*kalpa*), and an unfailing, unimpeded accomplishment in every respect. There will be the accomplishment of attracting all merit, and the supreme accomplishment of the rituals for the maṇḍalas, mudrās, and chapters. One will enter into the secret pledges (*samaya*) of the family of all the Tathāgatas.

Having kindled a fire with fuel-sticks of *khadira* and *nimba* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of salt mixed with rice, sesame, mustard seeds, curd, and ghee. All obstacles, *vināyakas*, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and planetary spirits (*grahas*), as well as all wicked adversaries and enemies, will be pacified. It delivers one from all quarrels, conflicts, and disputes. Victory shall prevail in all battles. It will grant victory over all foreign armies, adversaries, and enemies.

§9 By means of a lotus-homa, one should offer eight thousand oblations of parched grain (*lāja*) smeared with sandalwood, curd, honey, and ghee. There will be great peace throughout all kingdoms, market towns, villages, cities, and districts for a full thousand *yojanas* in every direction. It will provide protection, defense, and guardianship for all beings—men, women, boys, and girls. Everywhere, all diseases will be pacified. All fierce beasts, venomous serpents, and malevolent creatures will become friendly. All kings, together with their kingdoms, harems, and retinues, will abide in well-being and security.

Having kindled a fire with fuel-sticks of *arka* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *mataṅga* seeds, mustard seeds, and parched rice mixed with ghee, along with *nāgapuṣpa* flowers. When this is done, unseasonable drought shall fall; thereafter, the great *nāgas* will release torrents of rain. They shall cause rain to fall according to one's desire for as long as required. All crops, forests, grasses, shrubs, medicinal herbs, and substances, as well as flowers and fruits, shall become perfectly full and thoroughly matured. All the great *nāga* kings, together with their retinues, shall be greatly gladdened. From time to time, they shall release torrents of rain according to the seasons.

§11 In the event of excessive rain, one should offer oblations eight thousand times with that very ash; it pacifies the excessive rain. One should offer oblations of parched grain, cow dung balls, and mustard seeds smeared with ghee and *caṇḍabīja* [seeds]; this wards off all winds and lightning, and a great boundary-binding is established for a thousand leagues in every direction. For the binding of wind, one should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds and rice; all wind-circles will be bound, even up to the Vairambha wind. For the binding of *nāgas*, however, by offering eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds and sesame, a twelve-year binding of *nāgas* will be accomplished.

§12 For the pacification of all diseases, one should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds smeared with ghee; this pacifies all diseases. To ward off the armies of enemy forces, having kindled a fire with *karavīra* wood, one should offer eight thousand oblations of neem leaves, salt, and husks; all enemy armies, adversaries, and foes will perish, and they shall not appear again for as long as one lives. This constitutes a binding of the directions for a thousand *yojanas* all around. One should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame, mustard seeds, parched rice, and lotus petals smeared with ghee; a great boundary-binding for a thousand *yojanas* all around will thus be established.

§13 For the binding of all *vināyakas*, one should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds, black sesame, and black beans smeared with ghee. This will effect the binding of all obstacles, *vināyakas*, Māras, and wicked *yakṣas* and *rākṣasas*. To expel *yakṣas*, one should offer eight thousand oblations of salt and oil smeared with the "seed of breaking" (*bhaṅgabīja*). All *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, *bhūtas*, *piśācas*, *apasmāras*, and so forth, shall emerge visibly before the eyes of all people. All plagues, calamities, misfortunes, and all fears shall be pacified; there shall be well-being in every respect.

§14 For the subjugation of Brahmins, one should offer eight thousand oblations of parched grain (*lāja*) and *arka* wood fuel smeared with ghee; all Brahmins will become submissive. For the subjugation of Kṣatriyas, one should offer eight thousand oblations of molasses, ghee, parched grain, and *arka* leaves; this will bring about the subjugation of all Kṣatriyas. For the subjugation of Śūdras, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *madanaphala* and *karṇikārikā*; this is the supreme accomplishment for the subjugation of all Śūdras. For the subjugation of Vaiśyas, one should offer eight thousand oblations of the three kinds of ghee smeared [with the aforementioned substances]; this brings about the subjugation of all Vaiśyas. One should offer eight thousand oblations of *jātī* flowers and *sumana* flowers smeared with ghee; this brings about the subjugation of all women. For the subjugation of maidens, one should offer eight thousand oblations of water-flowers smeared with ghee; this will bring about the subjugation of all maidens.

§15 To pacify all fears, one should offer eight thousand oblations of rice and ghee; this will pacify all fears arising from strife, quarrels, conflict, and disputes. To increase wealth and grain, one should offer eight thousand oblations of seven kinds of grains mixed with ghee; there will be an increase in wealth and grain.

§16 For the attainment of sovereignty, one should offer eight thousand oblations of mustard seeds and honey; there will be a great increase in sovereignty. For the attainment of a territory, one should offer eight thousand oblations of the three pungents, ghee, and honey; there will be the acquisition of a great territory. For the sake of a village, one should offer eight thousand oblations of *karavīraka* flowers, mustard seeds, parched grain, and ghee; one will obtain a village. For the excavation of a treasure, one should offer eight thousand oblations of lotus stalks smeared with ghee; one obtains a great treasure.

§17 One who desires to summon a yakṣa should offer eight thousand oblations of guggulu, caṇḍabījaka, honey, and clarified butter. The yakṣa will appear before him in his own form. He will become a servant, performing all tasks.

§18 One who desires to summon a being capable of assuming any form at will (*kāmarūpin*) should offer eight thousand oblations of parched grain, mustard seeds, and *priyaṅgu* flowers, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. Having kindled the fire with fuel-sticks of *karavīra* wood, a being capable of assuming any form at will then arrives. He provides whatever one desires. Three types [of women] may be requested: a mother, a wife, or a sister. If it is a mother, through her maternal affection, she brings about an increase in great wealth, grain, and enjoyments; for as long as one lives, she remains free from deficiency. If it is a wife, she attends to one’s enjoyment through manifold and diverse amorous sports; she attends to one’s enjoyment of various garments, ornaments, decorations, perfumes, garlands, ointments, drinks, foods, and the finest varieties of diverse flavors. She attends to the increase of various beds, seats, wealth, grain, treasuries, and storehouses. For as long as one lives, she will follow one like a shadow; she would even sacrifice her own life [for him]. If it is a sister, then she attends to one’s enjoyment of various sovereign powers and celestial palaces (*vimāna*); for as long as one lives, she performs service and attendance.

§19 For the quelling of enemy armies, by means of an oblation of husks and salt, no enemy shall arise within a distance of one hundred thousand *yojanas*. One should offer eight thousand oblations; victory in great battles and conflicts will ensue.

§20 For the descent of the Sun, one should offer oblations of honey, salt, rice, and ghee. On a mountain peak, one should offer eight thousand oblations. Day after day, the Sun descends. He grants all boons and attends upon [the practitioner] with service and attendance that fulfills all desires for as long as life lasts.

§21 One who desires to cause the moon, the planets, and the host of stars to descend should offer oblations in a high place, using the three pungents (*trikaṭuka*), rock salt (*saindhava*), milk, honey, and ghee. The moon, the planets, and the host of stars will descend. They bestow the great increase of all desired objects, mental wishes, enjoyments, and sovereignty. They attend upon [the practitioner] for as long as life lasts; they provide protection, defense, and guardianship for as long as life lasts; and day by day, they descend with a desire to be seen.

§22 For the purpose of summoning all—gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans; women, men, boys, and girls; śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas; kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras—one should offer eight thousand oblations of sesame, mustard seeds, rice, and all medicinal herbs, smeared with curd, honey, and ghee. There will be a great accomplishment of summoning. One will become beloved by the whole world. Kings, together with their harems and retinues, will come under one’s control. They will remain constantly attached to that very person and will follow one’s word, whether in matters of self or wealth. One will be universally esteemed as the foremost teacher and worthy of great honor.
§23 The accomplishment of the ritual procedure for the fire offering (homa).
